title: Outcome, process, or balancing?
brief:
A primary care team has set the aim: ‘Reduce the proportion of children under five who leave the clinic without their complete vaccination card updated, from 30% to under 10% within six months.’

A balanced family of measures usually has 1–2 outcome measures, 3–5 process measures, and 1–2 balancing measures. Match each candidate measure to its type.

task.stem: Match each candidate measure to its role in the family.

items.label: Proportion of under-five children leaving the clinic without an updated vaccination card.
Proportion of visits where the vaccination card is checked at intake.
Average minutes from arrival to vaccination card review.
Average waiting time per visit (to ensure the new step does not lengthen visits unduly).

debrief.correct: Good. The aim names the outcome (cards updated). Process measures look at how the system performs (cards checked at intake, time to review). Balancing measures watch for unintended consequences elsewhere — here, total waiting time.
debrief.wrong: Trace each measure back to the aim. Outcome = what we ultimately want to change (cards updated). Process = how the system is performing (cards checked, time to review). Balancing = what else might get worse if we focus only on the aim (waiting time).
debrief.rule_cited: Family of measures — IHI Model for Improvement (QI 102 / QI 103).
